question: Why do self-supervised methods bother with proxy tasks instead of training directly on the downstream task?
direct_answer: Because proxy tasks provide supervision when labels are scarce or unavailable and help the model learn general features first.
expanded_answer: The proxy task gives the model a dense training signal from every unlabeled example. By learning patterns such as context, correspondence, or invariances, the encoder often discovers structure that transfers better than training from scratch on a small labeled dataset. The point is to shape the representation space, not just to solve the proxy task quickly.
key_points: Pretraining helps transfer to many downstream tasks
common_wrong_ideas: Proxy tasks are only a workaround and never improve performance
The proxy task must match the downstream task exactly
More labels always make self-supervision unnecessary
